messages:
Elaine (PM): Quick sync — we need a decision on the Priority Routing add-on credits model. Two options: 1) credits roll over month-to-month, 2) credits expire at month end or have a fixed TTL (e.g. 12 months). Pros/cons? Need launch criteria and contract implications.
Mike P.: My take: rollover is friendlier for customers and reduces churn, but adds product + billing complexity. UI will need balance display, and ops needs to cap accumulation.
Jordan / Sales: Customers ask for rollover all the time, especially startups — it’s an easy win in sales. Competitors offer 6–12mo rollover or lumps that expire; we get asked to match. :thinking_face:
Ana (Finance): Rollover creates deferred revenue nuances. Prepaid credits that never expire push recognition out longer. If we allow indefinite rollover we risk treating credits as liabilities for a long time. 12mo expiry is cleaner for ASC 606.
Mike P.: Also product-wise, indefinite rollover means unbounded state per account. We can mitigate with a hard cap (e.g., 5x monthly allowance) or expiry. Implementing cap + expiry keeps both sides happy.
Jordan / Sales: Can we offer grandfathered rollover for pilot/enterprise customers via contract amendment? Sales argues that for larger deals rollover is a negotiation lever.
Ana (Finance): Yes, but any exception requires explicit contract language and revenue recognition notes. We need a PR template and a finance sign-off for amendments.
sre-bot: FYI deploy note — billing feature flag for "credits_rollover" exists; toggle deploy is ~2h, needs migration script if enabled.
Elaine (PM): Proposed compromise: default product behavior = 12mo expiry from issuance + ability to configure expiry or caps on Dedicated/Private via contract. Pilot program: opt-in rollover (up to 12mo) behind a beta flag; requires contract amendment and finance approval. Launch criteria: docs + billing migration tested in staging, SLA for edge cases, and sample customer comms.
Jordan / Sales: Need a short field messaging line we can use in proposals.
Elaine (PM): Draft: "Credits issued with Priority Routing expire after 12 months by default. Enterprise customers may request custom expiry or accumulation caps via contract."
Mike P.: Quick calc for sales: if monthly plan = $10k and add-on credits = $2k/mo, rollover up to 12mo means potential $24k outstanding credits. With a 3% churn expectation, expected liability exposure = $720/yr per such account — manageable but flag to finance.
Ana (Finance): Please convert that into a proforma for 5, 50, 500-seat scenarios before next week.
Elaine (PM): OK — will file product spec PR with those constraints and pilot checklist. Decision target: lock policy and PR by EOD Friday so engineering can schedule the flag deploy next sprint. :white_check_mark:
